title: Val Thorens après-ski: La Folie Douce, bars, clubs and restaurants
metaTitle: Val Thorens après-ski: Folie Douce, bars, nightlife | SkiShare
description: Val Thorens après-ski starts at La Folie Douce on the slopes and ends in the village bars and clubs. Where to go, where to eat and quiet evenings in 2026/27.
keywords: things to do in val thorens at night
intro: Après-ski in Val Thorens has two stages: the afternoon on the slopes at La Folie Douce, at the top of the Plein Sud chairlift (2,600 m), with live music every day until the pistes close, then the evening in the village, which Les 3 Vallées says you can cross on foot in about twenty minutes. To eat, there are mountain restaurants up to Caron 3200 at 3,200 m, village restaurants such as the Michelin-starred Les Explorateurs (30 seats, booking essential) and the Sherpa supermarket for a raclette at home. We give times only where an official page publishes them for winter 2026/27; the lifts run from 21 November 2026 to 2 May 2027.

sections.heading: Where and when does après-ski happen in Val Thorens?
paragraphs: In two stages: on the pistes in the afternoon, then in the village in the evening. La Folie Douce has live music every day and, in its own words, people 'dance on the tables until the closing of the slopes'; in the village, says Les 3 Vallées, the bars get the evening going and the clubs take over after dark.

after: It is all within walking distance: Les 3 Vallées counts six areas (Soleil, Grande Rue, Balcons, Lombarde, Slalom and Plein Sud), crossed on foot in about twenty minutes, with a free bus between them.

sections.heading: La Folie Douce Val Thorens: where is it, and how do you get back down?
paragraphs: La Folie Douce is on the pistes at the top of the Plein Sud chairlift, at 2,600 m according to its own site, about 300 m above the village. It promises 'great live music every day', from electro and funk to house and rock, on a terrace 'often bathed in sunshine', and a VIP terrace closer to the artists can be booked.

**Food:** La Fruitière is the sit-down restaurant ('semi-gastronomic', it says) and takes bookings, La Petite Cuisine is the self-service, and the Folie Food Ratrack sells burgers, hot dogs and bagels.

**Opening times:** its site shows daily times, but the menus posted there are still last winter's (2025/26), so check [its après-ski page](https://www.lafoliedouce.com/en/val-thorens-apres-ski-clubbing.html) for this winter.

**Getting back:** ski down while the pistes are open, and plan that run before the last drink. SETAM, the lift company, warns on its [2026/27 beginners' map](https://ski.valthorens.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/PlanEasyRider-2027-MockUp-Web-ValTho_compressed.pdf) that 'the slopes are not for après-ski' because 'piste groomers are at work', and Les 3 Vallées advises checking the lift closing times on its [live page](https://www.les3vallees.com/en/live/lifts-and-trails-opening/val-thorens) before your last run.
**Not skiing?** The Plein Sud chairlift is not among the lifts SETAM opens to pedestrians, so ask La Folie Douce how a non-skier can reach it.

sections.heading: Bars, pubs and clubs in Val Thorens
paragraphs: Les 3 Vallées' [guide to going out](https://www.les3vallees.com/en/experiences/where-to-go-out-in-val-thorens) lists three clubs, two bars and two pubs; valthorens.com, the tourist office's site, adds Favela. What the sources say:

after: **Hotel bars:** Le 1971, at Le Val Thorens hotel on Place de l'Eglise, pairs a seventies-style bar and fireplace with a big terrace on the slopes, and the hotel promises DJ sets and après-ski. For a quieter drink, the Pashmina hotel's Lounge Bar, 'open to everyone', serves cocktails, wine and tapas with live music several nights a week.
**No hours here, on purpose:** no official page gives these venues' hours for 2026/27, and most of the listings above carry no date, so check each venue's own site or social pages before you go.

after: **Or picnic:** SETAM lists picnic tables and public toilets on the slopes, and Les 3 Vallées picks four [picnic spots](https://www.les3vallees.com/en/experiences/our-best-3-vallees-picnic-spots) in Val Thorens: La Ruche at the top of the Moutière chairlift, and the Goitschel (on the Goitschel red run), Rosaël (at 3,000 m) and Plateaux (by the snowpark) picnic chalets.

sections.heading: Restaurants in the village: do you need to book?
paragraphs: In peak season, yes. Les 3 Vallées advises booking lunch on the slopes ahead, 'especially during school holidays', and the Pashmina hotel calls booking its own restaurants 'strongly recommended, especially during peak season' and essential at its Michelin-starred Les Explorateurs, which seats only thirty.
**Savoyard food** means cheese: Les 3 Vallées suggests a fondue, a raclette or a reblochonnade, and Le Zinc serves Savoyard fondues.
**Dinner before a night out:** Yuki Yama, the Asian restaurant paired with Le Jackie, or Favela in Galerie Péclet, whose tacos, burritos and empanadas valthorens.com suggests before partying.

**Groups:** book before you travel, above all for New Year and the February school holidays, when the French zones take turns between 6 February and 8 March 2027 and England has its half-term. In our apartments, the weeks from 13 February to 6 March and New Year week are the dearest of the season; the holiday dates are in [when to go to Val Thorens](/en/guide/best-time-to-ski-in-val-thorens).

sections.heading: Food shopping for a self-catered apartment
paragraphs: Val Thorens has a Sherpa supermarket by the Place Péclet shuttle stop, a food shop 'tailor-made' for ski holidays in the tourist office's words, with butchery-rotisserie, charcuterie, cheese and local specialities counters, bread and pastries baked on site, a wine and spirits cellar, newspapers, snow chains and baby products.
**Raclette at home:** Sherpa sells ready-to-go raclette, fondue and hot-stone sets and lends the equipment; it also takes orders on sherpa.net and offers home delivery.

**Arrival day:** the tourist office's page gives no opening hours, so check them before you set off, especially if you arrive late on a Saturday. On our [apartments page](/en/apartments), agency apartments are rented by the full week, Saturday to Saturday, and SkiShare's own apartments by the night, for the dates you choose.

after: Cosmojet and the karting run depend on the weather and snow, and SETAM suggests contacting it a few days ahead. SETAM sells lift passes at its ticket offices and on ski.valthorens.com; this winter's prices are in our [lift pass guide](/en/guide/val-thorens-ski-pass-prices).

**Slower evenings:** dinner at the Chalet de la Marine or the Chalet des 2 Lacs, by tracked vehicle; the pool, saunas, hammam and cold plunge pool of [Le Board](https://www.sportwellnesslesbelleville.com/en/lieux/le-board/), the sports and wellness centre in the heart of the resort (check its winter hours); or a raclette at home.

sections.heading: Getting home safely after a night out
paragraphs: On foot, mostly: Val Thorens Réservation, the resort's booking agency, says you can do everything on foot. If you can, change out of ski boots and into snow boots before a long evening.

**The free shuttle** links the areas, but the timetable on [Les 3 Vallées' shuttle page](https://www.les3vallees.com/en/guide/shuttle-in-stations) carries no year (its season dates are those of winter 2023/24), so check live times and stops in the Zenbus app, which that page points to, before you rely on it late at night.

sections.heading: Where to stay for après-ski, and apartments by the week
paragraphs: Choose your area to suit your evenings: Val Thorens Réservation calls Grande Rue, right in the centre, lively in the evening, Slalom very quiet, and Balcons and Plein Sud, at the top of the resort, quiet. The six areas compared: [where to stay in Val Thorens](/en/guide/where-to-stay-in-val-thorens).

faqs.q: Where is La Folie Douce in Val Thorens?
faqs.a: On the pistes at the top of the Plein Sud chairlift, at 2,600 m according to its own site, about 300 m above the village. You ski back down to the village before the pistes close.

faqs.q: What time is après-ski at La Folie Douce Val Thorens?
faqs.a: According to La Folie Douce, you dance on the tables until the slopes close. Its site shows daily times, but in October 2026 it still carried last winter's menus, so check its 2026/27 times before you go.

faqs.q: What clubs are there in Val Thorens?
faqs.a: Les 3 Vallées lists three: Le Malaysia, an underground club beneath the main square; Klub Summit, in the central bar district; and Le Jackie, paired with the Asian restaurant Yuki Yama.

faqs.q: Do you need to book restaurants in Val Thorens?
faqs.a: In peak season, yes: Les 3 Vallées advises booking lunch on the slopes ahead, especially in the school holidays, and the Pashmina hotel strongly recommends booking its restaurants; its Michelin-starred Les Explorateurs, with 30 seats, requires it. Dinner at the Chalet de la Marine and the Chalet des 2 Lacs is by booking, with the ride up by tracked vehicle.

faqs.q: Is there a supermarket in Val Thorens?
faqs.a: Yes: Sherpa, by the Place Péclet shuttle stop, with butchery and cheese counters, bread baked on site, and raclette and fondue sets with the equipment lent. Its tourist-office page gives no opening hours, so check them before you arrive.

faqs.q: What can you do in the evening in Val Thorens if you don't party?
faqs.a: Ski until 6.30pm at Péclet by Night on Wednesdays from 10 February to 21 April 2027, take the Cosmojet toboggan run by head torch from Wednesday to Friday (from the Christmas holidays, with at least 40 people registered), try Kart Xperience, or book dinner at a mountain chalet.

faqs.q: Can you ski back down after La Folie Douce?
faqs.a: Yes, while the pistes are open. SETAM, the lift company, warns that skiing after they close is dangerous because the piste groomers are at work.
